content: Low magnesium levels in the blood can lead to symptoms such as muscle cramps, fatigue, irritability, and depression. If these symptoms persist or worsen, consult your doctor. Common side effects of magnesium supplements include stomach upset and diarrhea. Taking the supplement with a meal can help minimize these effects. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Before starting a magnesium supplement, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Some forms of this product, such as liquids or powders, may contain sugar, aspartame, or alcohol. Use caution if you have conditions like diabetes, alcohol dependence, liver disease, or phenylketonuria (PKU), or if you need to limit or avoid these substances in your diet. During pregnancy, magnesium supplements should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this product passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before use if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Magnesium can bind with certain medications, such as tetracycline antibiotics (e.g., demeclocycline, doxycycline, minocycline, tetracycline), reducing their absorption. If you are taking such medications, separate the timing of your doses by at least 2 to 3 hours. Check the labels of all your medications, including antacids, laxatives, and vitamins, as they may contain magnesium. In case of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., magnesium blood levels, kidney function) should be performed to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Magnesium supplements are available in various forms and dosages, many of which can be purchased without a prescription. Maintain a well-balanced diet to support your health. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this product at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
